lines.x: Were you looking for these documents, Professor? Here you are. I personally believe that some of these theories aren't explained in enough detail. If you wanted a springboard for your ideas, I suggest referencing these two papers. I've added some of my own commentary, so feel free to look it over.

The little lamb didn't go away even after the volcano erupted. It's actually been staying with me the whole time, and sometimes gets into trouble. H-Hey, you can't go standing on the Doctor's head! That's terribly rude! Sorry, Professor. Um, Can you see the little lamb? It's right here, hand to the right, and then down a little. Yeah, you're petting it right now.

This coat was Mom's old protective gear. Professor Keller once told me, this mark came from a sudden burst of magma. It almost left a scar on her, but Mom just laughed, saying she had good luck. If I were to go on an expedition with her, I'd probably need to be the one to lead.

Shh. Here, Professor, I snuck these over! I saw it all – you were muttering about how badly you wanted some snacks earlier, right? I've actually gotten pretty good at reading lips. Not to brag, but I might be better than Rhodes Island's intelligence agents by now. But, just maybe.

I'm getting ready to head out, Professor. Another volcano is about to become active. While luck is still on my side, I need to go a bit farther, a bit deeper. I want to wear the brightly-colored ornaments, and get to the truth in the hot magma, just like Mom and Dad did.

Professor, in a few days, I'll be going to Leithanien to attend a press conference and the premiere of my documentary. Our research is too obscure for the ordinary people who want to learn about volcanoes. But I still hope that one day, I can use this method to show everyone the beauty of volcanoes.

Frostleaf has been going to Mousse's book club a lot these days. Earthspirit and Provence have been trekking far and wide. I've been exploring more volcanoes... Professor, I still remember those early days, when Mousse was so nervous she couldn't even talk, and Frostleaf was always alone. But look at them now... they're getting better.

Hehe, Mr. Kahn's letter just arrived. He says he's really mad that Professor Keller and I went rowing on a sulfuric acid lake without protective gear. Mom and Dad did crazy things just like that before they had me, and they didn't bring Professor Keller along. So this time, so I took her with me!

One moment, Professor, I'm changing out my hearing aid battery. Hmm? You're... Did you forget, Professor? I can read lips now. Besides, the sign you want should be like this, then this. What you just did was 'I have been suppressed by the volcano.'
Phew... Even without my hearing aid, I can still pick up the little sounds of Professor's breathing…

Professor, I'm back, and I brought some souvenirs for you. I'll send them over to Dr. Kal'tsit and Amiya in a bit. I also managed to get a good amount of new data and specimens from Siesta's volcanic eruption. Would you like to come and take a look with me?
A volcano's every change and movement is fleeting. Only by capturing them on camera are we able to preserve every last detail.

Our documentaries are being taken seriously? That's great! During my inspections in recent years, I've seen a lot of governments that don't trust our judgment and won't allocate resources to evacuate the residents. I hope I'll be able to make a difference.
I know what you want to say, Professor, but I've never made my expeditions hard for myself. Starting from the smallest example, I bet you've never fried a fowlbeast egg over lava before, but I have!
How about a slice of lava cake before we head out? It was one of Mom's traditions.
Volcano field investigations are extremely dangerous. Everyone, please follow my instructions.
Please double check your protective gear. Also, remember to keep a safe distance from the lava, and give regular status reports.
Relax, volcano. We're just here to collect a few precious samples. Please don't get mad.
This time, we can make up for the missing data in the last report.
Don't worry about me, Professor. I've scaled a lot more volcanoes than you can imagine.
Volcanic soot contains lots of Originium particles. Let's not stay too long.
Magma will dredge up Originium veins. Keep your distance.
Melt away, life-depriving stone...
Ashes from volcanoes, they consume and erase, then nourish and propagate.
Those particles have no place here. I'll send them away.
Oh, flowing magma, please slow your steps.
We are one step closer to the truth of this land, Professor.
Perhaps there will still be people gazing across this volcano a century from now. Their footprints will cover ours, and the seeds buried beneath the ash will bloom into even more beautiful flowers...
Why…? I'm not seeing any errors in the formula or the data... Um? I think I see something surfing through the lava...?
Phew... Thankfully, the volcano didn't want to keep me that badly.
Professor, I brought the documents you asked me about.
I heard you coming, Professor. I recognized your footsteps.
Professor, I know how good you are at learning. I can tell you're doing the wrong sign on purpose just to make me laugh!
Arknights.

A pebble encounters countless other pebbles during its life. They will collide with each other and become magma. When they reach critical temperature, they erupt. In the end, they turn into the ash that nourishes new life. We're just like these little pebbles, Professor– Oh! Why didn't you tell me the fireworks already started?!
Professor, the fault lines of mountain ranges and trenches are quietly moving beneath our feet. Little by little, they inch us closer to the volcanoes we hope to visit.

The obsidian in this brooch comes from a volcano you haven't climbed yet. When you're not busy, we can go volcano-climbing. We'll visit the volcanoes one by one. And you'll know exactly which volcano I'm talking about once you get to the top. The scenery up there is magnificent, and the other half of your present is waiting for you.

Professor, I read in a book that after thousands of years, we will all re-enter this land's cycle. Maybe I'll become a little plume of magma, reshaping the land along its rock formations. When that time comes, I'll be able to forever look out across the land, with what nourished me, nestling up against me.

sets.name: A Picnic Before A Long Trip

lines.x: Mmm~I smell whipped cream. Look, the lambs have started their picnic over there. Care to join them with me, Professor?

Professor, would you like to try this cupcake I made? It's got a small piece of berry, some cream I scooped from a bigger cake, and the plate is a vine leaf… Why is there a lamb hiding in your hood...? This must be one of Dolly's pranks.

What do you think of my dress, Professor? Is the ribbon tied right? The lambs invited me to a party, but all they gave me to wear was a big ball of wool! Rather naughty of them, don't you think? It's been so long since I danced in a dress. I'm worried I might have some trouble. Would you mind practicing with me?

Hm? What was that, Professor? Sorry, I didn't quite catch that, please wait a second... My, how did this wool get in my ear? It must have slipped when I was playing hide-and-seek with the lambs! Go ahead, Professor, I can hear you now.

We've come pretty far, haven't we, Professor? A little fowlbeast brought me a rock from an acid lake. A little musbeast led me across an ocean of pink. And I even went aboard a great ship made of love and warmth. With these treasures, I don't feel at all lonely.

Do you like this cake, Professor? It's not just a regular cake. The base is made of love and dedication. The cream is distilled from our adventures. Various emotions are sprinkled as a finishing touch. And I've placed it in a box made of memories. It took me a long time to learn to bake a cake like this, Professor. I hope you'll remember the taste forever.
The little lambs can't wait to take us out to play again. What did you think of the chocolate lava in that volcano earlier? I much prefer the crystal candy from the thermal lake myself.

Phew. Looks like the sun's about to set. If only we could catch up with it, then the picnic could go on a little longer. How nice it would be if we could dance in a circle and sing. Pretty sun, warm sun, why you set so soon? Please stay, please wait, for time is such a boon♪

Cotton drifting on♪ We fly like clouds and chase the sun♪ Over the lava spout♪ We can't stop while the sun is out♪ Slow down if you please♪ You need to grant our wishes three♪ North Wind, make us rain♪ Bloom hot flowers from pebble grains♪
Shh... Listen carefully, Professor. That's the sound of flowers blooming... So soft and gentle. I'm glad I can hear it.
Is this a dream? A cozy, cloud-white dream?
I wonder if anyone recorded the picnics, too?
The flowers will not wither, and the sunlight will be forever warm. If only we could stay in this moment…
Look, professor! The hills are covered with Volcano Watchers! It's beautiful! Ah, mom and dad are there, too! Hm? You don't see them?
The picnic's about to begin.
Yes? You're putting me in charge of the picnic?
Come quick, Professor! There's still a ripe berry on that vine!
The little lambs say it's fun to roll around on the clouds. Do you think we can go for a picnic up there?
I hear fowlbeasts flapping their wings.
The rainbow bridge rises between the clouds.
The lava surges on, never turning back.
A pebble returns to her hometown.
A cotton candy cloud, drizzled in azure sky syrup.
A sweet-and-sour rainbow, dipped in golden sunshine.
A refreshing breeze, mixed into bubbling soda.
Sleep now, and fall into a sweet dream.
Hand in hand we stride, singing atop the gentle clouds.
Ring-a-ding-ding, when the flowers gently fall, the berries you can haul.
Oops, be careful now. Sudden shrinking takes some getting used to. Try not to trip and fall, okay?
Oh my, who knocked over the cake stand? The lambs' faces are covered in cream!
Can I bring the cake in?
Hey, quit it, little lamb. Oh, it's you, professor.
The lambs and I have matching bow ties. Aren't they pretty?
Arknights.

I think it's snowing on those hills in the distance… Are you cold, Professor? The fairy tales say you can spin snow into nice, soft robes. Those who wear them will sleep the gentlest of sleeps. I hope you too will have sweet dreams tonight.
Professor, since we've shrunk and the desserts haven't... Maybe we can keep eating as much as we want?

You've finally reached the top of the volcano, Professor. This is the view I've always wanted to show you... Why are you dreaming of me? Hehe, it's my way of telling you what I want to say. Happy birthday, Professor.

Mhmm... It's so quiet here. The sun is as warm as ever, and the breeze is always gentle. Professor, we may go on separate journeys from here, but don't worry. Even if we part ways for now, there will come a day when we meet again.
